reason: Google Pay top-up failing fits both the Apple/Google Pay intent (dataset convention for Google Pay top-up issues) and top_up_failed.
No beneficiary is mentioned; 'account not allowing transfers' is a generic declined/failed transfer, so beneficiary_not_allowed assumes context the text lacks.
A pure 'how long does delivery take' question is the delivery-estimate intent, not a card-not-arrived status query.
Asks how many virtual cards one gets, not about disposable card limits; the message never says disposable.
Lost wallet plus unrecognised withdrawals; blocking the lost card and disputing withdrawals are both defensible readings.
User already did a card top-up and the money vanished; that is a failed top-up, not a how-to-top-up-by-card question (and not a bank transfer).
Generic 'will a transfer incur a fee' fits transfer_fee_charged literally, while the dataset files SEPA/SWIFT fee questions under top_up_by_bank_transfer_charge.
Asks to check an exchange rate is correct with no mention of cash withdrawal; a generic exchange-rate query, gold assumes unstated context.
Unrecognised transactions plus explicit 'my card must be compromised, freeze it'; both intents are defensible.
'When will my transfer go through' can be a pending specific transfer or a generic timing question.
Asks when funds will transfer; nothing about a recipient not receiving money.
Generic 'how long do transfers take' is transfer_timing, not a recipient-did-not-receive complaint.
An in-app currency exchange that cost too much; no card payment is involved.
Stolen wallet and someone withdrawing money; both the stolen-card and unrecognised-withdrawal intents are defensible.
'Will I get a real card' is get_physical_card literally, but order_physical_card is a near-duplicate intent.
Asking whether salary is eligible (to be received into the account) is receiving_money; source-of-funds verification is not what is asked.
Generic question about how long a transfer takes to show, no specific pending transfer.
'Top up did not complete' reads as failed but could equally be a pending top-up.
Waiting a week on a seller for money back; could be requesting a refund or chasing a refund not showing up.
Top-up already made but not visible; a pending top-up, not a how-to-top-up-by-card question.
'I made a transfer and it hasn't gone through' with no direction stated; pending outgoing transfer or incoming balance not updated.
Asks about using American Express to top up, which is both a supported-cards question and a top-up-by-card how-to.
Using the card abroad in Germany is card_acceptance; country_support is about where the service is offered.
Generic 'how long until a transfer reaches the recipient' is timing, not a complaint that money was not received.
Asks whether SWIFT transfers are supported; no mention of charges.
SEPA transfer fee question; dataset convention files it under top-up-by-bank-transfer charge, but transfer_fee_charged is defensible literally.
'Unable to make a transfer to another account' has no beneficiary-not-allowed context; a failed transfer.
Reports an incoming UK bank transfer not appearing but explicitly asks for the typical time frame; both fit.
'How do I get an actual card' is get_physical_card literally; order_physical_card is a near-duplicate.
Top-up not showing in wallet is a pending top-up, not a how-to-top-up-by-card question.
Card not working in a shop fits both card_not_working and declined_card_payment.
Money left the account but the seller never received it; nothing about a reverted card payment.
Asks whether SWIFT transfers are possible; no fee question.
'Take money from my card' with the transaction pending is a pending cash withdrawal, not a card payment.
A generic unexplained fee on the account; nothing ties it to a card payment.
'Total cost of a transfer' is a generic transfer fee question; gold reflects the dataset's bank-transfer fee convention.
Reactivating a found card is activate_my_card; card_linking (linking a card to the app) does not match the request.
Generic how-to-top-up question; card top-up and bank transfer into account are both defensible.
Getting a paycheck into the account is receiving_money, but transfer_into_account is defensible.
Asks whether multiple transactions are possible with a virtual card (single-use limit question); nothing says the card is not working.
In-app RUB to GBP exchange charged too much; no card payment involved.
A 'cancelled' card payment could be reverted or declined.
'How long should my new card take to arrive' is a delivery estimate question.
A large charge the user did not make with no mention of a direct debit; card payment not recognised.

Lost wallet and withdrawals started; both stolen-card and unrecognised-withdrawal readings are defensible.
Top-up done but not showing yet is a pending top-up, not a how-to question.
Card declined when buying online is a declined card payment, not a declined transfer.
Generic 'what extra charges are there' has no transfer context.
Refusing to verify identity is closest to why_verify_identity (is it required); the user is not unable to verify.

'I need a physical card' fits both order_physical_card and get_physical_card.

Charges made on the user's card by someone else; explicitly card payments, not a direct debit.
Changing USD to EUR is both an in-app exchange how-to and a supported-currency question.
Checking whether a top-up worked; verify_top_up fits and top_up_failed is a defensible dataset reading.
Complains about ATM withdrawal charges/fees; no exchange rate is mentioned.
App will not let the user buy crypto; an in-app exchange issue, not a beneficiary restriction.

When an incoming transfer will be available; timing question or balance not updated.

How long for transferred money to show up; timing or incoming balance not updated.

Unrecognised 'payment' to cancel; card payment or direct debit not distinguishable from the text.

Generic top-up methods question; nothing about cash or cheque.
How to check the rate applied to a transaction; no claim of a wrong card-payment rate, so a generic exchange rate question.
The card was cancelled, not a payment reverted; card_not_working is the closest intent.

Cards stolen, not a phone.
